blocks.note: first meaning: barely, by the narrowest margin
second meaning: a win earned with nothing to spare

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning reads as a sports report: a victory that was deserved, though only by a whisker.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an adverb meaning barely, and also describes a result earned with no margin to spare.

blocks.note: first meaning: to arrest, in slang
second meaning: condition

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the outline of a bust or chest; both words are slang. 'In good nick' is British for in good condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Police slang uses the verb for arresting someone, and British idiom uses the noun for physical condition.

blocks.note: surface reading: somewhere young goats might be penned or roam
setter's reading: kids are children, and hanging out is spending idle time with friends in a club for teenagers

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'kids' and 'hang out' are to be taken in their casual sense: a community building where young people socialise.
explanation.definitionFit: A community facility for young people is exactly a place for teenagers to spend leisure time together.

clue.text: To get knots out of short line

indicators.note: something short is lacking its end, so the final letter of the preceding phrase's word is cut

blocks.note: to untie something is to remove its knots
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Someone trying to untangle a length of rope that is too short to manage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To' is the definition, in the sense of 'from nine to five'; 'short' trims the untying word before the line letter is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words act as prepositions marking a time limit, as in 'open from nine to five' or 'open until five'.

clue.text: Hot sandwich in oven couple will eat

indicators.note: whoever eats something takes it inside, so the following piece goes within the couple word

blocks.note: to couple things is to tie them together
an oast is a kiln for drying hops

explanation.surface: A snack being heated in the oven that a pair of people are about to share.
explanation.walkthrough: An oast is a hop-drying kiln, common in Kent, so an oven in crossword terms.
explanation.definitionFit: A toastie is British for a toasted sandwich, typically filled with cheese and served warm.

clue.text: Figure of speech describing posh company

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to trace round it, so one word is drawn around another

blocks.note: a trope is a figurative use of language
U means upper-class, the classic posh label

explanation.surface: A metaphor used to characterise an upper-class firm or circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Describing' is used in its geometric sense of drawing round. U for upper-class comes from the 1950s 'U and non-U' usage debate.
explanation.definitionFit: A troupe is a touring group of actors or performers, which is a theatrical company.

indicators.note: something cutting into another piece goes inside it, so one piece is set within the next

blocks.note: taken as written
a lance is a long spear carried by a horseman
ER is Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A command to hand a blade to Her Majesty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give' looks like a verb but is the noun: the amount of slack or flex something allows. The queen goes inside the weapon after the plain 'to'.
explanation.definitionFit: In engineering, the allowed variation or slack in a part is its tolerance, the same as its give.

indicators.note: when a person leaves, he is no longer present, so those two letters are taken away

blocks.note: O looks like zero, nothing
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone left with nothing once a man walks out.
explanation.definitionFit: To own something is to possess it, which is one sense of the verb to have.

clue.text: Seeds taken from outside to be put in bowls

indicators.note: pieces put in something are placed within it, so they go inside the following word

blocks.note: something taken from outside is brought in
taken as written
pans are shallow bowls or basins

explanation.surface: Seeds collected outdoors and brought in to be placed in dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' plus 'to be' sit inside the bowls word, between its first letter and the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinto beans are mottled kidney beans, the seeds of a bean plant used in Mexican cooking.

indicators.note: something returning goes back the way it came, so the abbreviation is read right to left
made short, the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: ca is circa, Latin for about
quite good means fairly good

explanation.surface: A defendant being let off after coming back to court rather quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquit someone is to clear them of a criminal charge by a verdict of not guilty.

clue.text: Zip turned into single multifunction device

indicators.note: turned round, the word is read backwards
one piece goes into another, so it sits inside the word that follows

blocks.note: zip is American slang for nothing, nil
single and alone both mean unaccompanied

explanation.surface: A zip fastener converted into one gadget that does several jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Zip' looks like a fastener but means zero; reversed, it goes inside the word for single, after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-in-one is a machine combining several functions, such as a printer that also scans and copies.

indicators.note: something shot is wrecked or ruined, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written: twelve letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A kidnapping and shooting out on the moors, like a grim crime report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' reads as gunfire in the crime story, but it is the signal that the letters are ruined and remade.
explanation.definitionFit: A kidnapped person is held to ransom, kept captive until money is paid for their release.

indicators.note: turned over, the phrase is flipped and read from the end

blocks.note: to sit on a decision is to stall over it
taken as written
usage is established custom, a rule of practice

explanation.surface: The Football Association delaying its decision on a rule change.
explanation.walkthrough: FA is not the Football Association but short for 'sweet FA', British slang for nothing at all. 'Stalled' is sat on, reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Both 'sweet FA' and the answer are British informal phrases meaning absolutely nothing.

clue.text: Clear story about social event finishing early

indicators.note: an event that finishes early is cut short, so its last letter goes
a word placed about another goes round it, enclosing it

blocks.note: an at-home is a party held in one's own house
a fable is a short moral story

explanation.surface: A plain tale about a party that wound up ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: The shortened at-home sits inside the story word straight after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fathomable can be understood, so it is clear in the sense of comprehensible.

blocks.note: fare is food, as on a menu
astern is nautical for at the rear of a ship

explanation.surface: Asian dishes served from the rear of the premises.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental describes things from East Asia, the region also called the Far East.

indicators.note: walls surround what they enclose, so the word goes round the other piece

blocks.note: to supplant is to take the place of
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone pleading for a person to rebuild the walls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Walls' looks like a noun but is the verb: the replacing word encloses the numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: A suppliant attitude is a humbly pleading one, so the adjective means begging.

indicators.note: finally points to the end of the word, so only its closing letter is kept

blocks.note: the closing letter of erect
a hem is the edge of a piece of cloth

explanation.surface: America's enemies putting up a frontier wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'US' is not the United States but the pronoun us, as in 'us and them'.
explanation.definitionFit: In 'us and them', the second pronoun means the opposing side, so it names those against us.

clue.text: Tiny amount of intelligence, you might say

indicators.note: what you might say is how a word is spoken, so its pronunciation counts, not its spelling

blocks.note: wit is quick intelligence

explanation.surface: A barely measurable quantity of brainpower.
explanation.walkthrough: For many speakers the two words sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A whit is the smallest particle, as in 'not a whit', meaning a very small amount.

clue.text: Having to take band's instruction to vocalist

blocks.note: a posse is a band of people, here possessive
what you tell a singer to do

explanation.surface: A musician obliged to follow the group's direction to the lead singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' suggests a pop group, but the band here is a posse, a gang of people.
explanation.definitionFit: Possessing and having both mean owning or holding something.

one word surrounding another wraps round it

blocks.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A wanted criminal who has nowhere to hide being a real problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retreat' looks like a verb next to 'can't', but it is the noun: a private refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: A sanctum is a private, quiet room where one can withdraw undisturbed, a retreat.

blocks.note: taken as written: twelve letters to rearrange

clue.text: Long period of time before November

blocks.note: a year is a period of time
N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A lengthy stretch of time leading up to November.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective about the period, but it is the verb to long.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something and to yearn for it both mean to desire it intensely.

blocks.note: first meaning: a pigeon-like bird, symbol of peace
second meaning: the past tense of dive, in American usage

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a bird plunging; one word is the bird and, pronounced differently, the past tense of dive.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names a white bird of the pigeon family; the verb form is the US past tense of plunge downwards.

blocks.note: first meaning: a verb, to extract or take away
second meaning: the opposite of concrete, existing only as an idea

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a builder declining to take out concrete; 'concrete' is the adjective meaning tangible.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to take out or extract; as an adjective it means conceptual, the opposite of tangible.

clue.text: I'm grateful for that good mark

blocks.note: ta is British informal for thank you
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Someone thankful for receiving a high grade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good mark' looks like a grade, but the definition is just 'mark'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tag is a label or identifying sign, a mark attached to something.

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

indicators.note: something dubious is not straight or reliable, so the letters are put in another order

blocks.note: taken as written
the answer to 17 across

clue.text: Played with king in rich surroundings

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it, surrounded by the other
surroundings enclose whatever is set within them, confirming which word is the outer one

blocks.note: moneyed means wealthy
K is king in chess notation
